name: Political Bias Detection
pitch: Reads a news headline, says whether it leans left, right or centre, and shows the words that drove the call.
description: A Social Computing course mini-project, done in a team of two. Headlines are turned into sentence embeddings, a classifier learns Left, Center and Right from labelled Kaggle datasets, and SHAP shows which words pushed a prediction. A Gradio app lets you upload training CSVs, train, type a headline and see the prediction, its confidence, a word-importance plot and the most similar headlines it was trained on. The proposal and literature survey are written up in the course slides; the notebook is the working prototype.
hardestProblem: Making the answer explainable instead of a bare label. The proposal argued that most bias detectors are black boxes and learn a publisher's style rather than real bias, so the prototype pairs every prediction with a SHAP word-importance plot and nearest training examples.
highlights: Literature survey of eight papers on political-bias detection, with gaps identified in each
Prototype: MiniLM embeddings with logistic regression (class-balanced) and a nearest-neighbour lookup for similar headlines
SHAP word-level explanations and a Gradio interface for training and testing
Original plan was to fine-tune BERT and predict framing, sensationalism and loaded language; the notebook is the simpler first version
